rows.jp: 今日から新学期。

ghs.en: The new school term starts today.

rows.jp: 女っ気のない当家におきましては、起床→通学過程における萌え要素は皆無ゆえ、いちいち思考をなぞることもなく、さっくり外に出た。
rows.en: With no women in the house, the journey from bed to school contains not one scrap of moe. No point retracing every thought. I head straight outside.

ghs.en: As waking up in a house with no female presence means the process of Wake Up → Go to School is wholly devoid of that moe factor, I lightly exit to outside without following each thought one by one.

rows.jp: 一ヶ月半ぶりの通学。
rows.en: My first walk to school in a month and a half.

ghs.en: Commuting to school after a month and a half.

rows.jp: いい天気だった。

ghs.en: Weather was nice.

rows.jp: まだ九月初頭なのに暑すぎることもない。
rows.en: Even in early September, it isn’t oppressively hot.

ghs.en: It's still the beginning of September, but it's not excessively hot.

rows.jp: 前髪がかすかにまぶたにかかる。
rows.en: My bangs just graze my eyelids.

ghs.en: My bangs hung hazily in front of my eyelids.

rows.jp: それだけが少し不快。
rows.en: That alone bothers me a little.

ghs.en: That's the only slight discomfort.

rows.jp: 「切っておきたかったなー……」

ghs.en: Taichi: "Awww, and I wanted to cut 'em..."

rows.jp: 鬱陶しい。

ghs.en: How gloomy.
ghs.assessment: In the immediate context of bothersome bangs, 鬱陶しい means annoying, bothersome, or irritating. 'Gloomy' instead describes mood or atmosphere and breaks the stated causal link to his hair.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Annoying' or 'What a nuisance.'

rows.jp: 色のせいもあるけど、あまり自分の髪は好きじゃない。
rows.en: Maybe it’s partly the color, but I’ve never much liked my hair.

ghs.en: I don't really like my hair, although it's a bit the color's fault.

rows.jp: 「はー」

ghs.en: Taichi: "Sigh..."

rows.jp: 前髪をいじりながら通学路に出た。
rows.en: Fiddling with my bangs, I set out along the road to school.

ghs.en: I began on the road to school as I played with my bangs.

rows.jp: てくてく歩く。

ghs.en: Trudging along.

rows.jp: 今度誰かに切ってもらうか。
rows.en: Maybe I’ll have someone cut it for me next time.

ghs.en: Should I get someone cut them for me sometime?

rows.jp: うん、そうしよう。

ghs.en: Yeah, I'll do that.

rows.jp: 「おいっす」

ghs.en: Girl: "Oi there!"

rows.jp: 「ちわっす」

ghs.en: Taichi: "Yo there."

rows.jp: 自転車に乗った少女が、ごく自然なタイミングで隣に並ぶ。
rows.en: A girl on a bicycle pulls alongside me at exactly the right moment.

ghs.en: A girl riding a bike lined up next to me with quite natural timing.

rows.jp: よたよたと、それでも器用にバランスを取りながら併走。
rows.en: She wobbles along at my side, deftly keeping her balance all the same.

ghs.en: She lines up to me with an unsteady yet skilfully kept balance.

rows.jp: 徒歩の速度でよくこけないもの。
rows.en: It is a wonder she can ride this slowly without falling over.

ghs.en: That's not something that falls easily to walking speeds.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese marvels that she manages not to topple over while riding at walking speed. The English instead describes an unspecified thing failing to reduce or 'fall' to walking speeds, reversing the physical event and losing the rider as subject.
ghs.remedy: Use 'I'm amazed she doesn't fall over at walking speed.'

rows.jp: 自転車はいかにも高そうなバイクタイプ。
rows.en: The bicycle is an expensive-looking mountain bike.

ghs.en: The type of bike seems to come with a very high price.

rows.jp: 快活そうな彼女には、よく似合ってる。

ghs.en: It's well suited to a girl that seems to be so lively.

rows.jp: 「よっと」

ghs.en: Girl: "Yott'oh!"

rows.jp: 軽くウイリーなどしてみせる。

ghs.en: She makes display of a little wheelie.

rows.jp: あ、パンツ見えた。

ghs.en: Ah, I saw her panties.

rows.jp: 白い。白すぎる。

ghs.en: White. Way too white.

rows.jp: 純白だ。

ghs.en: Pure white.

rows.jp: やっぱ純白ってのがいいなあ。すごくいいなあ。
rows.en: Pure white really is the best. So, so good.

ghs.en: Yep, pure white is so goood. So awesooome.

rows.jp: もっと見たいなぁ。

ghs.en: I wanna see mooore.

rows.jp: あ、もう見えないや。

ghs.en: Ah, I can't see them anymore, no.

rows.jp: がっくし。

ghs.en: Dammit.

rows.jp: 「ねえ、たいっちゃん裏山って行ったことある？」
rows.en: “Hey, Tai, have you ever been up the hill behind the school?”

ghs.en: Girl: "Say, Taicchan, you ever been to the forest heart of the mountain?"
ghs.assessment: 裏山 is the hill or mountain behind a place, conventionally the nearby back hill. The English invents a forest and relocates the destination to a mountain's interior or heart, neither of which is stated.
ghs.remedy: Use 'the hill out back' or 'the mountain behind here,' according to the established geography.

rows.jp: 一枚の布きれで男心を見事にくすぐった少女は、首だけでこっちを向いた。
rows.en: Having worked such wonders on the male heart with a single scrap of cloth, she turns just her head toward me.

ghs.en: This girl whose one thin scrap of cloth so magnificently tickled my male spirits turned just her head towards me.

rows.jp: 「あるよ。こないだまで合宿してた」
rows.en: “I have. I was camping there until the other day.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "I have. We were having club training camp up until recently."

rows.jp: 「夏休み中？」

ghs.en: Girl: "On your Summer Break?"

rows.jp: 「そう」

ghs.en: Taichi: "Yep."

rows.jp: 「……ふーん、それでか」

ghs.en: Girl: "...uhhh-huh, maybe that's why."

rows.jp: 「それでって、なにが？」

ghs.en: Taichi: "That's why, what?"

rows.jp: 「いや、あの一帯ってさ、神様がいるんだよね」
rows.en: “Well, you know, there’s a god in that whole area.”

ghs.en: Girl: "Nah, it's just that in that area, there's a god there y'know."

rows.jp: 二人はしばし見つめあった。
rows.en: For a moment, we stare at each other.

ghs.en: Our two gazes locked for a brief moment.

rows.jp: そして突然同時に。
rows.en: Then, at precisely the same instant—

ghs.en: Then suddenly and simultaneously,

rows.jp: 「わははははは」

ghs.en: Taichi: "Wahahahahahah!"

rows.jp: 「あははははは」

ghs.en: Girl: "Ahahahahahah!"

rows.jp: 「わはははははははははは」

ghs.en: Taichi: "Wahahahahahahahahahahah!"

rows.jp: 「あはははははははははは」

ghs.en: Girl: "Ahahahahahahahahahahah!"

rows.jp: 「もんのすごい御利益があるわけさ」

ghs.en: Girl: "He's got this amazing graciousness, y'know."
ghs.assessment: 御利益 is a divine or religious benefit, blessing, or efficacy granted by a deity or sacred site. 'Graciousness' instead describes a person's courteous or merciful character and loses the promised benefit.
ghs.remedy: Say that the deity brings extraordinary blessings or benefits.

rows.jp: 「何事もなく続けないように」
rows.en: “Don’t just carry on like nothing happened.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "I wish you wouldn't just go on like nothing happened."

rows.jp: 「いや、笑いたくなるのはごもっともですよ。あたしだって人からンなこと真顔で言われたら笑うわ」
rows.en: “Look, I get why you'd laugh. If someone told me that with a straight face, I'd laugh too.”

ghs.en: Girl: "Naaah, wanting to ridicule it is totally natural. If some guy saidd'at to me with a really straight face I'd laugh too."
ghs.assessment: 笑いたくなる means feeling the urge to laugh. 'Wanting to ridicule it' adds an intention to mock or belittle something, changing an involuntary comic reaction into directed scorn.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Of course you'd want to laugh' or equivalent.

rows.jp: 「だから俺を笑かすために真顔だったのだろうに」
rows.en: “That’s why you kept a straight face—to make me laugh.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Therefore you just said that to me with a straight face to make me laugh, have you."

rows.jp: 「そうだけど……でもちょっと真面目な話なんよ、これ」
rows.en: “Well, yeah... but this is kind of serious.”

ghs.en: Girl: "Right, but... this is still sort of a serious thing, this is."

rows.jp: 「神様が？」

ghs.en: Taichi: "The god?"

rows.jp: 「そう」

ghs.en: Girl: "Yep."

rows.jp: 「神様って英語で言ったらゴッドなんだぜ？」
rows.en: “You know what you call a god in English? God.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "The kind of thing that in English you'd spell G-O-D?"

rows.jp: 二人はしばし見つめあった。
rows.en: For a moment, we stare at each other.

ghs.en: Our two gazes locked for a brief moment.

rows.jp: 「わははははは」

ghs.en: Taichi: "Wahahahahahah!"

rows.jp: 「あははははは」

ghs.en: Girl: "Ahahahahahah!"

rows.jp: 「わはははははははははは」

ghs.en: Taichi: "Wahahahahahahahahahahah!"

rows.jp: 「あはははははははははは」

ghs.en: Girl: "Ahahahahahahahahahahah!"

rows.jp: 「……話すすまないよぅ（泣）」
rows.en: “...We're never going to get anywhere like this. *sob*”

ghs.en: Girl: "...we're talking in circles now (sob)."

rows.jp: 「よしよし、聞いてあげるから。なに、神様がどうしたって？　そもそもそれはどんな神なの？」
rows.en: “There, there. I'll listen now. What about this god? What kind of god is it, anyway?”

ghs.en: Taichi: "There, there, I'll listen to you then. So, what's it all about with this god? In the first place, which god are we talking about?"

rows.jp: 「あー、それは七香さんも知らないな」

ghs.en: Girl: "Ahhh, that, Nanaka-san doesn't know either, no."
Taichi: "Wha-...?!"

rows.jp: その瞬間、俺はピンと来た。
rows.en: In that instant, it comes to me.

ghs.en: In that instant, I knew, instinctively.

rows.jp: 「おい大発見。漢字で書くよりひらがなで『ななか』って方が萌えないか！？」
rows.en: “Major discovery: isn't your name much cuter written as ‘nanaka’ instead of in kanji!?”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Whoa, grand discovery! If you write the name "Nanaka" in hiragana instead of the kanji for "seven" and "scent", it's way more moe, isn't it?!"

rows.jp: 「知ってる」

ghs.en: Nanaka: "Knew it."
ghs.assessment: 知ってる is the blunt present-state reply 'I know' or 'I already know.' 'Knew it' instead means a prior suspicion has just been confirmed, changing the response's temporal and pragmatic force.
ghs.remedy: Use 'I know.'

rows.jp: しれっと言う。
rows.en: She says it without missing a beat.

ghs.en: So she says all nonchalant.

rows.jp: 唐突な路線変更にめげるタイプではないらしい。
rows.en: Apparently, abrupt changes of subject don’t faze her.

ghs.en: Doesn't seem to be the type that flinches in front of sudden swerves in the train of conversation.

rows.jp: 「ほら、ほこらあるでしょ。ほこら」
rows.en: “You know the little shrine up there. The hokora.”

ghs.en: Nanaka: "Ahem, there's a hokora there. Ho-ko-ra!"

rows.jp: 「ホコラってカタカナで書くと感染力の高い病気みたいだよね」
rows.en: “Write HOKORA in all caps and it looks like the name of some highly contagious disease.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Writing 'hokora' in Katakana makes it sound like some incredibly epidemic disease, doesn't it."

rows.jp: 「ほら、ほこらあるでしょ。ほこら」
rows.en: “You know the little shrine up there. The hokora.”

ghs.en: Nanaka: "Ahem! There's a hokora there! HO-KO-RA!"

rows.jp: 二度も乗る気はないらしい。
rows.en: She is not taking the bait twice.

ghs.en: Even the second time she seems to have no interested in switching to my track.

rows.jp: 「林道の脇にある？」

ghs.en: Taichi: "Is it on the side of the mountain trail?"
ghs.assessment: 林道 is a forest or logging road, normally a road through managed woodland rather than a mountain footpath. 'Mountain trail' changes both the terrain and the kind of route.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Is it beside the forest road?'

rows.jp: 「そーそー」

ghs.en: Nanaka: "Yeppy yep!"

rows.jp: 「ほっ！」

ghs.en: Nanaka: "Hop!"

rows.jp: 自転車が再度ウイリーして、さらに後輪だけで跳ねた。
rows.en: The bicycle pops another wheelie, then hops on its rear wheel alone.

ghs.en: Once more the bike popped a wheelie, and this time also a big bunny-hop with the rear wheel.

rows.jp: 何の脈絡もないが、なかなかの技だ。
rows.en: Entirely unprompted, but a pretty good trick.

ghs.en: It may be out of the context of our talks, but that's still quite an expert trick.

rows.jp: 「ゴイシャス」%N※ゴイス（凄い）＋デリシャス
「だろー」

ghs.en: Nanaka: "Innit!"

rows.jp: 誇らしげな笑顔。

ghs.en: With a triumphant smile.

rows.jp: ここだけの話、ちょっと惚れた。
rows.en: Between you and me, I fall for her a little.

ghs.en: Just between you and me, that's quite charming.
ghs.assessment: ちょっと惚れた says the narrator fell for her a little or was briefly smitten. 'That's quite charming' transfers the state from his attraction to a judgment about an unspecified act and substantially weakens the confession.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Between you and me, I fell for her a little.'

rows.jp: 「ほこらの神様ってのが激ゴイシャスでさ」
rows.en: “The god in that shrine is seriously amazelicious.”

ghs.en: Nanaka: "The god of the Hokora is super gorgicious you know."

rows.jp: 「核戦争がおこっても守ってくれちゃうくらい御利益があるって話だ」
rows.en: “They say its blessings are strong enough to protect you even if nuclear war breaks out.”

ghs.en: Nanaka: "They say even if we have a nuclear war, his tender grace is so great that it will totally protect you."
ghs.assessment: 御利益 again denotes the shrine or deity's protective efficacy or blessings, not a male figure's tender graciousness. The possessive pronoun also fixes a gender absent from the Japanese.
ghs.remedy: Say that its blessings are supposedly powerful enough to protect someone even in a nuclear war.

rows.jp: 「嘘くさー」

ghs.en: Taichi: "All lieees."

rows.jp: 「どんなガン保険も本気を出したガンには無力なもんだよ」
rows.en: “Every cancer policy in the world is powerless once cancer gets serious.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Even if a cancer insurance gave all it had, it's still powerless in front of cancer!"
ghs.assessment: 本気を出した modifies the cancer: any insurance is powerless once cancer becomes serious or shows its full force. The English makes the insurance exert itself instead, reversing which side of the comparison intensifies.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Any cancer insurance is powerless once the cancer gets serious.'

highlights.text: Even if a cancer insurance gave all it had

rows.jp: 「いや、論点ずれてるし」
rows.en: “That has absolutely nothing to do with this.”

ghs.en: Nanaka: "No, yer slipping off of the point."

rows.jp: 「２１世紀の神様はもっとミニマムかつピンポイントでいいんですよ」
rows.en: “A twenty-first-century god should be smaller-scale and more precisely targeted.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "The god of the 21st century ought be much more minimalist and furthermore given to pin-point accuracy!"

rows.jp: 「彼女が自分よりかっこいい男にふたまたかけて肉体関係が発生した時に、携帯メールでそのことをリークしてくれる神様とかね」
rows.en: “Like a god who texts you when your girlfriend starts sleeping with a better-looking guy behind your back.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "A god who'll snitch to you with a message on your cellphone when your girlfriend two-times you with a guy cooler than you and is about to have a sexual relationship with him."

rows.jp: 「それ肯定できちゃうくらい権利意識が細分化してる社会ってのも、末期的だよね」
rows.en: “Any society atomized enough to recognize that as a legitimate divine portfolio is already terminal.”

ghs.en: Nanaka: "A society with a sense of entitlement so refined that it can assert to something so specific has to be on its death throes."
ghs.assessment: 肯定できちゃう means being able to approve, endorse, or accept that proposal. 'Assert to something' has no corresponding English relation and loses the claim that atomized rights-consciousness could make such a service socially affirmable.
ghs.remedy: Say that a society whose sense of rights is fragmented enough to endorse something so specific is already terminal.

highlights.text: can assert to something so specific

rows.jp: 「日本は冷静に狂ってるからね」
rows.en: “Japan is insane in a very levelheaded way.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Japan is calmly mad, that's why."

rows.jp: 「セヤッ」

ghs.en: Nanaka: "S'yah!"

rows.jp: 今度は前輪で倒立する。
rows.en: This time she stands the bike on its front wheel.

ghs.en: This time she made the bike stand on the front wheel.

rows.jp: これは驚く。

ghs.en: This one's astonishing.

rows.jp: 「うわ、その自転車すごいな！」

ghs.en: Taichi: "Whoa, that bike's amazing!"

rows.jp: 「自転車の方かい……」

ghs.en: Nanaka: "The bike, he says..."

rows.jp: 「乗らせて、乗らせて！」
rows.en: “Let me ride it! Come on, let me!”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Lemme ride it, lemme ride it!"

rows.jp: 「駄目。素人お断り」

ghs.en: Nanaka: "Nooo way. Amateurs rejected!"

rows.jp: 「ひどい」

ghs.en: Taichi: "Meanie!"

rows.jp: 「前も父が勝手に乗ってくれちゃってさー」
rows.en: “My dad took it for a spin without asking once.”

ghs.en: Nanaka: "Some time ago, dad helped himself to a ride without permission too."

rows.jp: 「しかも転んで傷つけて戻ってきてさ」
rows.en: “Then he wiped out, scratched it up, and brought it back.”

ghs.en: Nanaka: "And then he came back all hurt after a fall."
ghs.assessment: 傷つけて has the father damage the bicycle after falling and then return with it. 'He came back all hurt' instead assigns the damage to the father himself and omits the damaged object.
ghs.remedy: Say that he fell, damaged it, and brought it back.

rows.jp: 「もー大喧嘩したねー」
rows.en: “We had a huge fight over it.”

ghs.en: Nanaka: "Ohhh what a big fight we had, us two!"

rows.jp: 「傷のこと問いつめたらしらばっくれるしね」
rows.en: “When I confronted him about the scratch, he played dumb.”

ghs.en: Nanaka: "He acted alll innocent when I asked him 'bout those scrapes."

rows.jp: 「……パパも大変なんだよ」

ghs.en: Taichi: "...papa's a big fuss as well."
ghs.assessment: パパも大変 says that Dad has it hard too or that being Dad is difficult. Calling him 'a big fuss' instead characterizes him as a nuisance and changes the predicate.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Dad has it rough too.'

rows.jp: 「母に言いつけたさ」

ghs.en: Nanaka: "That's what mom always says."
ghs.assessment: 母に marks Mother as the recipient of 言いつけた: the speaker told or tattled to Mother. The English invents a habitual statement made by Mother and reverses the direction of speech.
ghs.remedy: Use 'So I told Mom on him.'

rows.jp: 「鬼か」

ghs.en: Taichi: "What a demon!"

rows.jp: 「父おこづかい三ヶ月減らされてやんの」
rows.en: “Mom docked his allowance for three months.”

ghs.en: Nanaka: "Daddy got his allowance cut for three months he did."

rows.jp: 「国民的家族像を思わせるシンプルな感情の流れだな」
rows.en: “A wonderfully simple emotional arc. The very picture of a wholesome family sitcom.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "That's the flow of simple emotions that reminds of the national ideal of a family."

rows.jp: 「ちょうどその時、父は同僚のパソコンにネットワーク経由で悪戯しかけてさ……卑語フォルダってのを自動生成するプログラムで相手の公開フォルダを卑語だらけにするっていう」
rows.en: “As it happened, right around then Dad was playing a prank on a coworker's computer over the network. He had this program that generated folders named after dirty words, flooding the other person's shared directory with obscenities.”

ghs.en: Nanaka: "Just around that time, daddy played a prank on a coworker's PC via the network... he went to use a program to automatically create folders labeled with swearwords to fill this guy's public folder with bad language!"

rows.jp: 子供おとなだ……。
rows.en: A child in a grown man’s body...

ghs.en: An adult child that guy...

rows.jp: 「ところが仕掛ける相手を間違えて、上司のパソコン卑語まみれ！」
rows.en: “Except he targeted the wrong computer and filled his boss's machine with obscenities!”

ghs.en: Nanaka: "But when he went to do it he got his target wrong, and he filled his superior's computer with swearwords!"

rows.jp: 「わははははは！」

ghs.en: Taichi: "Waaahahahahaha!"

rows.jp: 「あははははは！」

ghs.en: Girl: "Aaahahahahaha!"

rows.jp: アホだこいつの親。

ghs.en: And these idiots had a child.
ghs.assessment: こいつの親 is this person's parent, syntactically the subject being called an idiot. The English instead invents plural idiots who produced a child, changing the referent, number, and proposition.
ghs.remedy: Use 'This girl's parent is an idiot.' or the contextually appropriate singular equivalent.

rows.jp: 「そんで仕事でも減俸三ヶ月くらってるの。もー母と大爆笑！」
rows.en: “So they docked his pay for three months at work too. Mom and I just about died laughing!”

ghs.en: Nanaka: "And because of that, he also got a salary cut for three months. Oh how mom blew up a laugh!"

rows.jp: 「……そんな家族ばっかりだったら世界も平和であるだろうに」
rows.en: “...If every family were like yours, the world might actually know peace.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "...the world would be in harmony if all families were like that."

rows.jp: 「ま、もうおらんがね」

ghs.en: Nanaka: "Well, they aren't anymore."
Taichi: "Eh?"

rows.jp: くいっ

ghs.en: Thwink,

rows.jp: また自転車でウイリーをした。

ghs.en: the bike made a wheelie again.

rows.jp: あ、パンツ見えた！
rows.en: Oh, I saw her panties again!

ghs.en: Ah, I saw her panties!

rows.jp: 再見！

ghs.en: Rediscovery!
ghs.assessment: 再見 here is a compact joke on seeing the same sight again. 'Rediscovery' means finding or recognizing something anew rather than seeing it again and loses the immediate visual repetition.
ghs.remedy: Use a compact visual reprise such as 'Behold, again!' or 'Another sighting!'

rows.jp: 「いよっと」

ghs.en: Nanaka: "Y'ott'o!"

rows.jp: また見えた、あっ、あああっ！！

ghs.en: I saw them again, ah, aaah!

ghs.en: AAAAAAAAAAAAAAH!!!

rows.en: Pure white pure white pure white pure white!!

ghs.en: SnowWhiteSnowWhiteSnowWhiteSnowWhite!!!

rows.en: Riding up riding up riding up!!

ghs.en: CamelToeCamelToeCamelToe!!!

rows.jp: 「うっ」

ghs.en: Taichi: "Ngh."

rows.jp: ひざまずいた。

ghs.en: I kneeled.

rows.jp: 「どうしたの？」

ghs.en: Nanaka: "What is it?"

rows.jp: 「……ちょっと知能下がりすぎてやばかった、今……」
rows.en: “...My intelligence dropped so low just now that I was in genuine danger...”

ghs.en: Taichi: "...that was bad right then, my intellect sorta descended down way low..."

rows.jp: 「あー、きみのちのーは不安定なのかね？」
rows.en: “Ohh? Does your brainpower go up and down?”

ghs.en: Nanaka: "Ahhh, it's your intellect that's unstable, is it?"

rows.jp: 「サドルってときに気持ちよかったりする方？」
rows.en: “Are you the type who sometimes finds a bicycle seat kind of... nice?”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Doesn't it at times feel good when you're saddling with a sad'O?"
ghs.assessment: The source asks whether the bicycle saddle sometimes feels good, exploiting the immediate eroticized bicycle context. The English invents an incoherent construction involving 'saddling' and a 'sad'O,' importing a sadism pun that is not grammatically present and obscuring the actual question.
ghs.remedy: Ask whether the saddle ever feels good, preserving the suggestive ambiguity without adding a sadist figure.

highlights.text: when you're saddling with a sad'O

rows.jp: 「はい？」

ghs.en: Nanaka: "What?"

rows.jp: 「なんでもない……忘れてくれ」

ghs.en: Taichi: "It's nothing... do forget it."

rows.jp: ようやく理性が戻ってきた。

ghs.en: At last my rationality came back.

rows.jp: どうも突発的なエロイベントに弱いな。
rows.en: Sudden erotic events really are my weakness.

ghs.en: I'm just so vulnerable to unforeseen erotic events.

rows.jp: 立ち上がる。

ghs.en: I stand.

rows.jp: 「さ、学校に行こう」

ghs.en: Taichi: "Well then, let's go to school."

rows.jp: 「どうして前屈みなの？」

ghs.en: Nanaka: "Why are you slouching there?"

rows.jp: 「……そんな幼女のような無垢な口調で問うのか」
rows.en: “...You ask that in the innocent voice of a little girl?”

ghs.en: Taichi: "...you're asking that with the pure tone of a little girl?"
Nanaka: "?"

rows.jp: 「極めて下方に関わる空間的な問題によって、としかコメントできないな」
rows.en: “All I can say is that I am contending with a spatial problem of an extremely lower nature.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Other than it is due to a spatial problem concerning my extreme lowermosts, I cannot comment."

rows.jp: 「腰が痛いんだ」

ghs.en: Nanaka: "Your groin hurts, is that it."
ghs.assessment: 腰 refers here to the waist, hips, or lower back, not the groin. The substitution makes the supposedly innocent diagnosis explicitly sexual and materially changes the exchange.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Your lower back hurts, is that it.'

rows.jp: 「だからおぼこは……」

ghs.en: Taichi: "Really, an oboko like you..."

rows.jp: 「おぼこってなに？」

ghs.en: Nanaka: "Oboko... what's that?"

rows.jp: 「腰が痛くてね」

ghs.en: Taichi: "My groin hurts, that's it."
ghs.assessment: The repeated 腰 again means the waist or lower back. Rendering it as 'groin' repeats the anatomical error and undermines the speaker's attempt to pass off his posture as an ordinary back complaint.
ghs.remedy: Use 'My lower back hurts, that's all.'

rows.jp: 「ふーん」

ghs.en: Nanaka: "Ohhh."

rows.jp: よし、ごまかした。

ghs.en: Great, swindled.

rows.jp: 「気をつけなよー。子孫繁栄がやばいぞ」
rows.en: “Careful. You’ll put the family line in jeopardy.”

ghs.en: Nanaka: "Take some care theeere! The safety of the offspring seems at risk!"
ghs.assessment: 子孫繁栄 concerns the future continuation or flourishing of one's descendants: his reproductive prospects are in danger. 'The safety of the offspring' instead implies danger to already existing children and changes the causal joke.
ghs.remedy: Warn that his future family line or ability to have children is at risk.

highlights.text: The safety of the offspring seems at risk

rows.jp: 「子孫作りてぇー」

ghs.en: Taichi: "Let's make some offspriiiing!"
ghs.assessment: 作りてぇ is the speaker's rough contraction of 'I want to make/have,' expressing his own desire. 'Let's make' turns that desire into an inclusive proposal to the listener and adds a target absent from the Japanese.
ghs.remedy: Use 'I wanna make some babies!' or an equivalent first-person desire.

rows.jp: 「呆れるほど欲望に正直な子だな」
rows.en: “You’re astonishingly honest about what you want.”

ghs.en: Nanaka: "A guy disgustingly honest with his desires, are you."

rows.jp: 「……不意を突かれると本音が出るんだ」
rows.en: “...Catch me off guard and the truth comes out.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "...my true motives come out when I'm taken by surprise."

rows.jp: さすがに今のは反省したくなった。
rows.en: Even I want to reflect on that one.

ghs.en: All the same, I wanted to take back that one right then.

rows.jp: 「どんな男だって可愛い女の子を見たら、むくむくと欲望が鎌首をもたげてレッドスネークカモンなんですよ」
rows.en: “Any man who sees a cute girl feels desire rear its head and goes, ‘Red Snake, come on!’”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Any sort of man, when he sees a cute girl, would see his desire toweringly rise its head, as assuredly as when you shout Red Snake C'mon!"

rows.jp: 「レッドスネークカモォンなんだよ、きみ」
rows.en: “Red Snake, come ooon, I tell you!”

ghs.en: Taichi: "And it's all a 'red snake, c'mon!' with you!"

rows.jp: 「あ、でも普段はブルースネークで安全なんですよ？」
rows.en: “But normally it's the Blue Snake, so it's perfectly safe. See?”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Ah, but usually it's the green snake, so you're safe, OK?"
ghs.assessment: ブルー is explicitly blue, not green. Changing the snake's color breaks the stated red-blue-yellow sequence that structures the surrounding joke.
ghs.remedy: Use 'blue snake.'

rows.jp: 「中間がイエロースネークだったり？」
rows.en: “And the one in the middle is the Yellow Snake?”

ghs.en: Nanaka: "Is there a huggy y-ero-w snake between them?"

rows.jp: 「そう、いわゆる半勃……」

ghs.en: Taichi: "Yes, what you'd call a half-erec---"

rows.jp: 言ってて自分で不安になった。

ghs.en: So I said, and became uneasy all on my own.

rows.jp: こわごわと振り返って、
rows.en: I look back at her, half afraid.

ghs.en: Timidly timidly I turned around.
Taichi: "...disgusted?"

rows.jp: 七香はにこりと笑う。

ghs.en: Nanaka laughed with a sweet smile.

rows.jp: 「ううん、嬉しい」

ghs.en: Nanaka: "Nh-nh, I'm happy."
Taichi: "Huh?"

rows.jp: 「ほらほら、歩く歩く」

ghs.en: Nanaka: "C'mon, c'mon! Walk, walk!"

rows.jp: 「海綿体がねんねするまで後ろ走ってあげるからさ」
rows.en: “I'll ride behind you until your erectile tissue goes back to sleep.”

ghs.en: Nanaka: "Until that erectile tissue goes nighty-night, I'll be riding behind you, OK?"

rows.jp: 「とうに気づいてるんじゃねぇかこのアマ……」

ghs.en: Taichi: "You noticed that from the start, dinn'cha, you nun..."
ghs.assessment: アマ in this colloquial katakana use is a derogatory term for a woman, roughly 'bitch' or 'damn woman,' not the religious noun 'nun.' The literal homophone erases the insult and produces an unrelated characterization.
ghs.remedy: Use an appropriately harsh insult directed at a woman.

rows.jp: 自転車事件の桜庭ばりに深い傷を負った。
rows.en: I suffer a wound as deep as Sakuraba's in the bicycle incident.

ghs.en: I suffered a deep wound of depth reminiscent to Sakuraba's with his bicycle affair.

rows.jp: 「おー、学校がー、見えて参りましたー♪」
rows.en: “Oh, the school has hove into view♪”

ghs.en: Nanaka: "Ohhhhh, the schoool, it has come into vieeew!♪"

rows.jp: 「白いねー、新しいねー、金かかってるねー」

ghs.en: Nanaka: "So white isn't iiit, so new isn't iiit, so expensive isn't iiit!"

rows.jp: 「転校してくる？」

ghs.en: Taichi: "Want to transfer in?"

rows.jp: 「今なら無試験で当日編入可」

ghs.en: Taichi: "Right now, you can get admitted same day as request, no entrance test required!"

rows.jp: 「制服は？」

ghs.en: Nanaka: "And the uniform?"

rows.jp: 「ぼ、ぼくが用意してあげげげげげ」

ghs.en: Taichi: "This, this harmless young boy will arrange it-it-it-it-it-it!"

rows.jp: 「……胸のところ丸く切り抜いた制服ダロ？」
rows.en: “...With round holes cut out over the breasts, right?”

ghs.en: Nanaka: "...heh, it's an uniform with round holes cut 'round the height of the chest, r-i-g-h-t?"

rows.jp: 「ヒィッ、そんな鬼畜なことしません！？」
rows.en: “Eek! I would never do anything that depraved!?”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Hyyy, I will not do such beastly things?!"

rows.jp: 「……ただスカートのサイズがその、丈が普通のより三センチ短いやつしかないんだ……そ、それでもよかったららら……」
rows.en: “...I just happen to have one with a skirt three centimeters shorter than standard... I-if that would be all right with you...”

ghs.en: Taichi: "...merely, ah, the skirt size is, hum, a thing about three centimeters shorter than the normal measure, nothing to do about it... ah, uhm, if for you that's alright-ait-ait-ait..."

rows.jp: 「根性のないセクハラだな……」

ghs.en: Nanaka: "This sexual harassment's got no bite..."

rows.jp: 「さってと、あたしもそろそろ行かないと」

ghs.en: Nanaka: "Well then, it's about time for me to get going."

rows.jp: くるりと自転車が回転する。その場で。
rows.en: Her bicycle pivots in a circle on the spot.

ghs.en: The bike abruptly spun around. On a dime.

rows.jp: 彼女の運動神経はちょっとしたものだった。

ghs.en: This girl's motor skills were quite the thing.

rows.jp: 「少年、裏山のほこらの話、あれホントなんだ」
rows.en: “Boy, what I told you about the shrine on the hill—that part is true.”

ghs.en: Nanaka: "Young boy, that thing about the hokora up the mountain, that's all true."
Taichi: "...eh?"

rows.jp: 言葉の意味が、なかなかのみこめなかった。
rows.en: It takes me some time to grasp what she means.

ghs.en: I wasn't quite able to understand the meaning of her words.

rows.jp: 「どうしても行き詰まったら……行ってごらん」
rows.en: “If you ever reach a point where you truly have nowhere left to turn... go there.”

ghs.en: Nanaka: "If you get totally stuck... please go there."
Taichi: "Uh, huh..."

rows.jp: ふっと、表情が曇る。
rows.en: Her expression clouds for an instant.

ghs.en: Her face clouds without warning.

rows.jp: 「こんなこと言っても、何が変わるってわけでもないんだけどさ」
rows.en: “Not that saying this is going to change anything.”

ghs.en: Nanaka: "But even if I tell you this, nothing at all will ever change, that's what."
Taichi: "Nanaka..."

rows.jp: 「おっと、シメっぽくなっちまいやがった、こいつぁいけねぇや」
rows.en: “Whoops, now we've gone and made things all maudlin. Can't have that.”

ghs.en: Nanaka: "Whoopsie, this turned all gloomy didn't it, that ain't gonna go!"

rows.jp: ウイリーしてその場でくるっと。
rows.en: She pops a wheelie and spins on the spot.

ghs.en: She spun around on the spot with a wheelie.

rows.jp: 一回転したときには、もう笑顔。
rows.en: By the time she completes the circle, she is smiling again.

ghs.en: And when she had spun around completely once, she was smiling again.

rows.jp: 「じゃーねぃ♪」

ghs.en: Nanaka: "Byez now!♪"

rows.jp: 束ねた指先を華麗に振って。
rows.en: She gives an elegant flutter of her gathered fingers.

ghs.en: Waving bundled up fingertips with magnificence,

rows.jp: 彼女は爪先をペダルにかけた。
rows.en: Then she sets her toe on the pedal.

ghs.en: the girl put her toes to the pedals.

rows.jp: 「あ、ひとつ質問」

ghs.en: Taichi: "Ah, I have one question."

rows.jp: 去っていく背中に。
rows.en: I call after her as she rides away.

ghs.en: To her departing back.

rows.jp: 「なぁにー？」

ghs.en: Nanaka: "Whaaat?

rows.jp: 「どうして初対面なのに、俺の名前知ってたの？」
rows.en: “If we've never met, how did you know my name?”

ghs.en: Taichi: "How is it that this was the first time we've met, but you knew my name?"

rows.jp: 「うむ。その質問に答えるには……」

ghs.en: Nanaka: "Hum. To answer that question..."

rows.jp: 白い指先が俺をびっと指す。
rows.en: A white fingertip snaps toward me.

ghs.en: A white fingertip shot out, pointed at me.

rows.jp: いや、俺の背後だ。

ghs.en: No, at something behind me.

rows.jp: 振り返って、視界が学校をとらえて数秒。
rows.en: I turn. The school fills my vision for several seconds.

ghs.en: Turning around, my field of vision was captured by the school for several moments.

rows.jp: 返事がない。

ghs.en: No answers there.

rows.jp: 目線を七香に戻す。

ghs.en: My gaze returned to Nanaka.

rows.jp: 彼女はいなくなっていた。

ghs.en: The girl had vanished,

rows.jp: 自転車とともに。

ghs.en: along with her bike.

rows.jp: 早いで済まされる現象ではないのだが。
rows.en: ‘Fast’ does not begin to explain it.

ghs.en: Not a Phenomenon that's going to be settled quickly.
ghs.assessment: 早いで済まされる means the event cannot be explained away merely by saying she was fast. The English instead says the phenomenon will not be resolved quickly, changing speed as an insufficient explanation into the time needed to settle a problem.
ghs.remedy: Use 'That was beyond anything you could explain by saying she was fast.'

highlights.text: Not a Phenomenon that's going to be settled quickly

ghs.en: Taichi: "......mother of...?"
ghs.assessment: The small-kana ぉゃ represents a subdued, puzzled おや—roughly 'huh?' or 'well?' It is not the noun 親 or a fragment meaning 'mother of,' so the English invents an unrelated phrase.
ghs.remedy: Use a quiet puzzled reaction such as '...Huh?'

rows.jp: 蝉も鳴いてない、静かな新学期だった。
rows.en: Not even the cicadas are singing. A quiet start to the new term.

ghs.en: It was a quiet new school term, when even the cicadas didn't cry.
